classification.difficultyReason: Select and connect several parallel-line converse/direct properties, auxiliary-line angle decomposition, point/reflex totals and unsignposted short equations across six configurations.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals in each of these diagrams.

spec.description: Three horizontal parallel rays (including the short leftward middle ray at U), two rising parallels, vertical perpendicular and descending transversal; all original labels retained.
spec.mathematics: Single arrows identify all three horizontal rays; double arrows identify the rising family. The5alpha sector is between the leftward middle horizontal ray and rising ray, supplementary to alpha. Thus6alpha180 and alpha30; beta56+30=86.

answer.worked:
The short horizontal ray at the vertex marked $5\alpha$ is parallel to both long horizontal lines. The rising lines are also parallel, so the marked obtuse angle and $\alpha$ are supplementary.
$$\begin{align*}5\alpha+\alpha&=180^\circ\\6\alpha&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=30^\circ\end{align*}$$
The descending transversal makes an acute angle of $180^\circ-124^\circ=56^\circ$ with a horizontal line. Hence $\beta=56^\circ+30^\circ=86^\circ$.

spec.description: Three shallow parallel lines and two steep parallel segments, right boundary, internal cross-segment and lower diagonal.
spec.mathematics: Three β sectors exhaust the angles at the left middle vertex. α and 97° are co-interior angles on the steep parallels.

answer.worked:
$3\beta=360^\circ$ (angles at a point), so $\beta=120^\circ$.
$\alpha=180^\circ-97^\circ=83^\circ$ (co-interior angles on the steep parallel lines).
The upper-left angle of the upper quadrilateral is $120^\circ$ by corresponding angles, and its lower-left angle is $180^\circ-97^\circ=83^\circ$.
$\gamma=360^\circ-120^\circ-74^\circ-83^\circ=83^\circ$ (angle sum of a quadrilateral).

spec.description: Angular outline with triple, double and single parallel families, an internal segment and reflex-angle mark.
spec.mathematics: 294° is the reflex angle at the upper-left vertex. 104° is below the internal segment against the downward left side.
spec.answerVisibility: Unknown α and β remain unfilled.

answer.worked:
The small angle at the upper-left vertex is $360^\circ-294^\circ=66^\circ$. Matching parallel lines give $\alpha=66^\circ$.
The upper triangle's lower-left angle is $180^\circ-104^\circ=76^\circ$.
Its remaining angle is $180^\circ-66^\circ-76^\circ=38^\circ$. The single-arrow parallel lines give $\beta=38^\circ$.

spec.description: Concave pentagon with extended top edge and two parallel families.
spec.mathematics: β denotes the smaller outside angle at the concave vertex, beneath the two lower edges.

answer.worked:
The acute angle between the two parallel families is $73^\circ$, so $\alpha=180^\circ-73^\circ=107^\circ$.
Through the concave vertex, draw a line parallel to the double-arrow sides. It divides the marked angle into angles equal to $73^\circ$ and $67^\circ$ by alternate angles.
$\beta=73^\circ+67^\circ=140^\circ$.

spec.description: Two unmarked lines crossed by rays from one lower vertex, with a leader identifying the 12° vertex angle.
spec.mathematics: No parallel arrows are supplied; parallelism must be inferred from 63°+117°=180°.

answer.worked:
$63^\circ+117^\circ=180^\circ$, so the two lines are parallel by the converse of the co-interior angle property.
The small triangle below the lower line has angles $117^\circ$, $12^\circ$ and $\alpha$; the last is vertically opposite the labelled angle.
$\alpha=180^\circ-117^\circ-12^\circ=51^\circ$.
$\beta=180^\circ-51^\circ=129^\circ$ (co-interior angles).

spec.description: Outer triangle, apex-to-exterior ray and crossing segment from its left side to the exterior point; leaders distinguish the two apex sectors.
spec.mathematics: 12° lies between the upper side and extra ray, 21° between that ray and the left side. Exterior-point reflex angle is 348°; lower crossing angle is 5α.

answer.worked:
The small angle at the exterior point is $360^\circ-348^\circ=12^\circ$.
In the triangle formed by the apex, left-side point and exterior point,
$\beta=180^\circ-21^\circ-12^\circ=147^\circ$.
The upper side and crossing segment are parallel because the extra ray makes equal alternate angles of $12^\circ$ with them. Thus $\alpha$ and $5\alpha$ are supplementary.
$$\begin{align*}6\alpha&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=30^\circ\end{align*}$$
